RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have decided
to open new Kendriya Vidyalayas in the
country during the Eleventh Five Year Plan;

poverty line

SHRI MOTIUR RAHMAN:
Will the Minister of MINORITY
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) the total number of minority
community population living below
poverty line in the country, State-wise;
(b) the total number of minority
population living below lower middle class
population in the country, State-wise; and

Supreme Court's direction on filling
up of vacant posts of judges
*364. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of LAW AND
JUSTICE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Supreme Court directed
on April 3, 2006 that most of the States
have so far failed to put in place a
mechanism to speedily determine and fill
up vacancies of judges at all levels of
judiciary;
(b) if so, whether the Union
Government has taken up this seriously
and has urged the States to recommend the
mechanism for speedy determination and
filling up of vacancies of judges at all levels
of judiciary; and
(c) if so, to what extent the Union
Government has agreed to help and assist
the States in filling up the vacancies of the
judges?
Lowest literacy districts in A.P.
*365. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that eight districts
of Andhra Pradesh have been identified as
having the lowest literacy rate;
(b) if so, the details of such districts;
(c) whether the above districts have
been identified under Special Literacy Drive
launched in April, 2005; and
(d) if so, to what extent this drive would
help to bring the above districts out of
'lowest literacy' tag?
Caste-specific UGC schemes
*366. SHRI S.M. LALJAN BASHA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether UGC has launched,
formulated, announced numerous caste-
specific fellowships, scholarships, grants,
financial aid, subsidies for individual
scholars and students and teachers in the
fiscal year  2006-07;
(b) the tabulated figures, numbers,
categories and other details for such schemes
of UGC related to caste-specific people in
2006-07;
(c) to what extent caste-specific
bonanzas will hurt minorities and their
educational aspirations; and
(d) the steps proposed to study the
long term impact of excluding minorities
from recent caste-specific bonanzas of
UGC?
Privatization of power distribution
*367. SHRIMATI HEMA MALINI:
Will  the Minister of POWER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that even after four
years of power privatization, Government
have not been able to produce desired results
in the Capital and the menace of inflated
bills and fast running meters are persisting;
(b) whether it is also a fact that
administration is not at all prepared to take
into account consumers' points of view;
(c) whether Government are taking any
steps to make Capital free from  power-
cut and no further increase in tariff;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?

115

Opening of IIT, Kharagpur campus in
Orissa

PANY:
MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the IIT, Kharagpur
proposes to open a campus in Orissa;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the time-frame within which the
campus would be opened?
Illegal mining in Delhi
†*369. SHRI BALAVANT ALIAS
BAL APTE:
SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS:
Will the Minister of MINES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
large-scale illegal mining at many places in
Delhi;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the details of action taken by
Government against those involved in illegal
mining;
(d) whether Government have made any
plan to check it; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Composition of female population
*370. SHRIMATI JAYA BACHCHAN:
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND
CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) the female population at present and
its composition, age-wise and its
deployment sector-wise;
(b) what are the emerging trends among
women in the cities and the country side;
and
(c) what is the approximate number of
women employed as well as working within
the confines of homes?
Expansion and development of food
processing industries
†*371. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
Will the Minister of FOOD
PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government have
introduced a scheme for expansion and
development of food processing industries
in the country since the last two years;
(b) if so, the number of food processing
units functioning in the country in March,
2004; and
(c) the total number of those units in
March, 2006?
State of power generation
*372. SHRI P.R. RAJAN: Will the
Minister of POWER be pleased to state:
(a) whether the present power
generation is in accordance with the Tenth
Five Year Plan target;
(b) if so, the details thereof including
the target and power generated during the
Tenth Five Year Plan, State-wise and
category-wise as on date;
(c) if not, the details of reasons for the
same;
(d) if so, whether there is any proposal
to diversify the energy sources; and

116
(e) if so, the details thereof and the steps
taken to implement the same?
Setting up of food processing
industries in Tamil Nadu
*373. SHRI THANGA TAMIL
SELVAN: Will the Minister of FOOD
PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
many varieties of fruits like, grapes,
mangoes, jackfruits, etc. are grown in large
quantities in Tamil Nadu;
(b) the steps taken by Government to
promote setting up of fruit-based food
processing industries in the State; and
(c) whether Government will pay
special attention to fruit growing districts
like Madurai, Theni, Dharmapuri etc. while
setting up food processing industries?
Implementation of recommendations
of Moily Committee
†*374. SHRI AMIR ALAM KHAN:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the efforts being made by
Government for implementing the
recommendations of Moily Committee on
the issue of 27 per cent reservation in higher
educational institutions and for gradual
increase in the capacity of the institutions;
(b) whether there are any guidelines to
ensure that there is no cut or loss of seats
for the students of general category;
(c) whether the system of reservation
would also be applicable in the case of
institutions engaged in higher research and
development;
(d) whether Government would
sanction grants for implementing
reservation in higher educational
institutions; and
(e) if so, the amount of grants for this
purpose and whether it would be included
in Budget proposals?
Foreign investment in food processing
industries
†*375.SHRI SHAHID SIDDIQUI:
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) the foreign investment made during
the last five years in the field of food
processing under the Ministry, year-wise;
(b) the names of States alongwith the
amount invested therein;
(c) the amount invested area-wise and
item-wise; and
(d) the number of projects commenced
so far out of the same?
Incidents of ragging
*376. SHRI B.J. PANDA: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether during the current academic
session, some ugly incidents of ragging have
been reported;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) what is the action plan of
Government to control this un-abated
menace;
(d) whether certain universities propose
to install CCTVs in the colleges to control
these incidents; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?

CHARJEE: Will the Minister of POWER
be pleased to state:

country is getting worse;
(b) if so, whether priority is to be given
for power generation in Tenth and Eleventh
Five Year Plans for power generation
capacity of 41000 and 51000 MW
respectively;
(c) whether States have also been
directed to make special efforts for taking
concrete steps in this direction; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Differences over mining policy
*378. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA:
Will the Minister of MINES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether hon'ble Prime Minister has
urged his Ministry to urgently sort out the
differences between the Centre and the
mineral-rich States with regard to value
addition of minerals within the State
boundaries and delays in the grant of
concessions by the State Governments;
(b) if so, whether he has started
consulting Chief Ministers of dissenting
States on these issues;
(c) whether the hon'ble Prime Minister
has also urged his Ministry to procure the
proposals based on the Hoda Committee
Report and frame a new policy; and
(d) the steps being considered to resolve
the issues and also to amend the Coal Mines
Act?
Mining lease proposals from Orissa
†*379. SHRI SURENDRA LATH: Will
the Minister of MINES be pleased to state:
(a) the number of proposals regarding
mining leases received from Orissa;
(b) the number of proposals sanctioned
out of them;
(c) the status of other proposals; and
(d) whether Government have fixed any
time limit to consider the pending
proposals?
Assistance for marriage of Scheduled
Caste girls
*380. SHRI TARIQ ANWAR: Will the
Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE AND
EMPOWERMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have decided to provide financial assistance
for the marriage of girl child belonging to
Scheduled Caste; and
(b) if so, the details thereof?

National Centre for Ocean Information

tide measuring instrument has also been

emergency crisis?

the Minister of EARTH SCIENCES be

Ministry;

(c) whether any steps have been taken

Universities in the country

MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is proposed to set up a
world class, multi-disciplinary Vedanta
university in Orissa;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether this institute of excellence
would be entirely in the private sector; and

cess amount indicating the specific 'heads'?

figures given in this report;
